Oral Judgment
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)

Though this appeal is listed for
admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2.  This appeal is by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 2.9.2021 passed in MVC No.1290/2018 on the file of learned II Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-XI Ballari1.
3.

Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, on 19.11.2018, one Bandi Meghanath along with his relative was proceeding by walk from Uravakonda town, near Palthuru cross, at that time, driver of Toyota Fortuner car bearing registration No.KA-34/N-5858 came from Ballari towards Ananthapuram in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to Bandi Meghanath from behind.
Due to which, Bandi Meghanath sustained grievous head injury and succumbed to the same at the spot.

The claimants being mother, nephew and 'Tribunal', for short NC:
2024:KHC-D:11551-DB niece of the deceased Bandi Meghanath filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
4. On appearance, respondent No.3/Insurer filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It is averred that the respondent No.1/driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and sought dismissal of the claim petition.
The Tribunal on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part by awarding total compensation of Rs.13,91,740/- with interest at 6% per annum.

5. Sri. Manjunath G. Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants submits that the Tribunal committed an error in deducting 50% of the assessed income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, without considering the fact that the claimants No.2 and 3 being nephew and niece of the deceased were residing with the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased, hence, they are required to be considered as dependents for the purpose of determining compensation.

He further submits that the Tribunal has considered the age of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:11551-DB deceased as 40 years taking note of Post Mortem report, however, Aadhar Card of the deceased indicates that his age was about 32 years at the time of his death.

He further submits that the Tribunal also committed an error in adding 25% of the assessed income towards loss of future prospects, since the deceased was below the age of 40 years, appropriate addition Smt. Bandi Ananthamma W/O Late Bandi ... vs Sri Bariki Mallappa S/O B. Linga Reddy on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135560934/
3 would be 40%.
Hence, he seeks to modify the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal to the aforesaid extent by allowing the appeal.

6. Per contra, Sri. Subhash J Baddi, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that there is no evidence whatsoever placed on record by the claimants with regard to the fact that the claimants No.2 and 3 were dependents of the deceased, except self-serving statement of claimant No.1/mother of the deceased.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly disbelieved the same and deducted 50% of the assessed income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

He further submits that in regard to age of the deceased, Aadhar Card and Post Mortem Report are two documents, which indicates two different age of NC: 2024:KHC-D:11551-DB the deceased, hence, the Tribunal has rightly considered the age of the deceased as 40 years.
Thus, he seeks to sustain the same.
He further submits that the claimants in the claim petition, age of the deceased is mentioned as 38 years.
Thus, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.
7. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
8. Undisputedly, in a road accident on 19.11.2018, deceased Bandi Meghanath sustained head injury and succumbed to the same at the spot.
The claim petition indicates that the deceased was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
However, Aadhar Card of the deceased indicates that the deceased was aged 32 years at the time of accident.

Hence, we are of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to accept the date of birth mentioned in the Aadhar Card of the deceased i.e., 32 years, in the absence of any dispute or challenge by the respondents.

Hence,
appropriate multiplier applicable would be 16.

Since the deceased was below the age of 40 years, the claimants would be entitled to addition of 40% of the assessed income towards loss of future prospects in light of decision of Hon'ble Apex NC: 2024:KHC-D:11551-DB Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2.
9.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as contention with regard to the claimants No.2 and 3 are the dependents of the deceased is concerned, the same cannot be accepted for the reason that the claimants have failed to prove the same before the Tribunal by adducing cogent and acceptable evidence.
Hence, we are of the considered view that the Tribunal has justified in deducting 50% of the assessed income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, which is unaltered.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to modified compensation under the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.11,750 + 40% x 12 x 16 x 50% = Rs.15,79,200/-
10.
Insofar as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under conventional heads is unaltered.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of of Rs.2,57,460/- (Rs.15,79,200 - Rs.13,21,740).
11.

In the result, we proceed to pass the following:

ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.

2017(16) SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11551-DB b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants would be entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.2,57,460/-, which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
c) The respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
d) The apportionment, deposit and  disbursement shall be made as per  award of the Tribunal.
e) Draw modified award accordingly.
f) No order as to costs.
